back: Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and arrange themselves as far apart as possible; lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs.
lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bonding pair > bonding pair–bonding pair

front: Shapes and angles with no lone pairs (2 to 6 pairs)?
back: 2 linear 180°; 3 trigonal planar 120°; 4 tetrahedral 109.5°; 5 trigonal bipyramidal 120° and 90°; 6 octahedral 90°.

front: How do you count electron pairs for an ion?
back: Central atom's outer electrons + 1 per singly bonded atom; add the negative charge or subtract the positive charge; divide by 2.

front: When is a molecule with polar bonds non-polar?
back: When its shape is symmetrical so the bond dipoles cancel (CO₂, BF₃, CCl₄).
